newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japanese firms expect solid profit growth in 96/97.
newsitem.headline: Japanese firms expect solid profit growth in 96/97.

text.p: Major Japanese companies expect solid profit growth in the current business year to March 31, a survey by the Tokyo Stock Exchange (TSE) showed on Thursday.
The exchange said that 1,275 big firms listed on the TSE expect total combined parent current profits of 9.92 trillion yen in the 1996/97 business year, up 8.06 percent from the previous year.
The companies' net profits, meanwhile, are expected to total 4.75 trillion yen, up 22.91 percent.
Banks and other financial institutions were not included in the survey.
The exchange based its figures on the firms' earnings forecasts in conjunction with their interim business result announcements.
However, the companies' total sales are expected to decline 1.56 percent from the previous year to 336.76 trillion yen.
Compared with the companies' forecasts six months ago, parent current profits were up 1.35 percent and sales were up 0.63 percent, but net profits were down 6.35 percent.

In a breakdown by sector, the machinery sector expects to see a 27.81 percent year-on-year increase in parent current profit to 473.4 billion yen, thanks to a recovery in capital investments and improved profitability in exports.
The figure is up 2.92 percent from the companies' forecasts six months ago.

However, the petroleum and coal sector expects a 25.27 percent decline in parent current profit to 57.1 billion yen, due mainly to the surge in oil prices. The figure is down 30.32 percent from the previous forecasts.
